::: {.callout-warning}
The selected grid row predates the current reaction-temperature record. Its
scores are historical and must not be read as scores for the current JSON. They
were calculated on a pre-greenfield Engine; the retained summary does not record

:::

# Question

Would a bounded change to CO₂ dispersion energy, coupled with an R4
carbamate-hydrolysis correlation, improve pressure and speciation together?

# Starting point and strategy

The screen compared direct Engine equilibria over 25 loading/temperature-spread
pressure states and 44 speciation states (131 positive species targets). The
broader final request covered 161 pressure observations at 40–120 °C from
Aronu, Hilliard, Idris, Jou, Mamun and Xu, plus Böttinger and Matin speciation
through 80 °C.

A 13-scenario refinement grid, nine local candidates and four final candidates
were compared. The selected row, `local-p0.15-db-350-eps+0.025`, combined a
2.5% CO₂ dispersion-energy increase with a 0.15 increase in the R4 pivot
$\ln K$ at 333.15 K and a −350 K slope change. This was a coupled data
calibration, not an optimizer estimate of CO₂ energy alone.

# Numerical result

The selected row evaluated 130/161 pressure observations with log₁₀ RMSE
**0.3540** and all 131/131 speciation targets with RMSE **0.2658**. A separate
two-start optimizer smoke attempt produced zero accepted starts and no fitted
values. The grid row therefore documents a bounded comparison rather than a
continuous estimate or confidence interval.

# Conclusion and limits

The screen supplied a useful direction for the exploratory bundle, but the
result cannot identify CO₂ dispersion independently of the R4 reaction
correlation. R4 was changed again by the later reaction-temperature fit, so
this page is provenance for the earlier starred CO₂ value rather than current
bundle validation. The retained pressure failures and lack of uncertainty
quantification also remain part of the result.
